title: On Delivering the letters before noon
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：deliver　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 deliver 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the keeper ① delivered the letters before noon in public, and every traveller in the tower said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the keeper ② delivers the letters before noon in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ deliver the letters before noon at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ delivered the letters before noon before — a line in the calendar for January 1943 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Delivering the letters before noon in public, the keeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ deliver the speech without one note in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Deliver the speech without one note at once and never mention it again.

By 1956 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the calendar, and a new traveller from the next tower ⑧ delivers the speech without one note in public every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stair, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ delivered the letters before noon again when nobody else would.

⑩ To deliver the letters before noon, my mother said in 1961, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the tower remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the tower forgets, somebody delivers the letters before noon in silence again and somebody must deliver the letters before noon in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 递送（一般过去式 delivered the letters before noon：1949 年守夜人头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 递送（一般现在 delivers the letters before noon：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 递送（不定式 to deliver the letters before noon：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 递送（过去完成时 had delivered the letters before noon：1943 年一月的年历上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 递送（动名词 delivering the letters before noon 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 发表（deliver the speech without one note：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去发表不看一个字讲完那番话）
G. v. 发表（deliver the speech without one note：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 递送（后段两处：新来的过路人照例 delivers the speech without one note，而母亲又一次 delivered the letters before noon）

items.q: to deliver the letters before noon

answers.why: deliver 意为“递送”，1949 年守夜人当着众人面递送午前把信送到，那是钟楼里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 delivered。
deliver 意为“递送”，自那以后守夜人一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 delivers。
deliver 意为“递送”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯递送午前把信送到”，此处为不定式 to deliver the letters before noon。
deliver 意为“递送”，年历里 一月 那行字说明早在 1956 年之前就有人递送过，故用过去完成时 had delivered。
deliver 意为“递送”，守夜人说“递送午前把信送到这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 delivering the letters before noon 作主语。
deliver 意为“发表”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去发表不看一个字讲完那番话”，should ever 之后用原形 deliver the speech without one note。
deliver 意为“发表”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻发表不看一个字讲完那番话（deliver the speech without one note at once），以后再也不要提起。
deliver 意为“递送”，新来的过路人每个年头都照例发表不看一个字讲完那番话，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 delivers。
deliver 意为“递送”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面递送午前把信送到，用一般过去式 delivered 叙述。
deliver 意为“递送”，结尾那句是母亲 1961 年的话：要递送午前把信送到，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和钟楼记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1949 年，守夜人当着众人面递送午前把信送到；钟楼里每一个过路人都说这是头一回。（delivered the letters before noon）
多年以后，守夜人仍一言不发地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（delivers the letters before noon）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯递送午前把信送到这件事本身。（to deliver the letters before noon）
早在 1943 年就有人递送午前把信送到，一月那天年历上的一行字就是证据。（had delivered the letters before noon）
守夜人说过，当着众人面递送午前把信送到这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（delivering the letters before noon 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻发表不看一个字讲完那番话，以后再也不要提起。（deliver the speech without one note，祈使句）
answers: In 1949 the keeper delivered the letters before noon in public, and every traveller in the tower said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three years on, the keeper still delivers the letters before noon in silence without being asked.
My mother said later that to deliver the letters before noon at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had delivered the letters before noon long before 1956, and the line in the calendar for January proves it.
Delivering the letters before noon in public, the keeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Deliver the speech without one note at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 deliver 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the keeper delivered the letters before noon in public, and nobody in the tower forgot it.
Even now the keeper delivers the letters before noon in silence whenever the tower asks.
Delivering the letters before noon in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever deliver the speech without one note in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next tower delivers the speech without one note in public every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother delivered the letters before noon again, and the tower remembered that half.
